name: Optimize GCS XML/native read-write wall-clock time

description: baseline harness failed to execute remote benchmark body

asi.hypothesis: Set up broad ch-builder benchmark for XML/native read-write paths
asi.failure_mode: kubectl exec omitted -i, so bash -s received no here-doc body and only the build/restart phase ran
asi.rollback_reason: No benchmark metrics were produced; pod had no /work/results/autoresearch_gcs_rw_* output directory
asi.next_action_hint: Add -i to kubectl exec for the remote benchmark here-doc and rerun baseline

description: second baseline attempt still did not run remote benchmark

asi.hypothesis: Remote benchmark should execute via stdin after build and restart
asi.failure_mode: autoresearch.sh still lacked kubectl exec -i after crash revert preserved the old script body; no /work/results/autoresearch_gcs_rw_* directory was created
asi.rollback_reason: No METRIC lines or benchmark output directory; only build/restart logs updated
asi.next_action_hint: Patch autoresearch.sh again, verify grep shows `kubectl exec -i`, then rerun baseline

description: successful broad baseline for GCS XML/native read-write suite

asi.hypothesis: Establish a broad non-overfit baseline covering real large part writes/reads and many-small-file writes/reads for xml, xml_64m20, and native
asi.benchmark_scope: real_write attaches 23.59 GiB source part to each object-storage disk; real_read scans heavy map/string columns; small workload copies and reads a 96-column local wide part
asi.best_initial_variant: xml_64m20 has lowest aggregate path time; xml is slowest largely due real_write and small_read
asi.next_action_hint: Inspect source for low-risk parameter changes; first try XML configuration variant or native/XML read buffer/client tuning that plausibly helps both real and small workloads

description: increase native gRPC compose upload concurrency from 4 to 8

asi.hypothesis: More native GCS temporary-object upload concurrency could reduce native real_write wall time without affecting XML paths
asi.outcome: Primary regressed from 659.404s to 699.528s despite real_write improving by about 16s; read phases regressed enough to dominate
asi.rollback_reason: Higher native upload concurrency is not a broad win on this suite and may add noise/resource pressure
asi.next_action_hint: Do not simply raise native max_concurrent_uploads globally; focus on read path or XML policy/client settings next

description: skip extra-byte range validation when native GCS read consumed requested limit

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding an extra read/status-drain probe after an exactly satisfied native GCS range read could reduce per-object read overhead without changing requested bytes
asi.outcome: Primary improved slightly from 659.404s to 656.218s; native aggregate improved, mostly via write/small read, but real_read was noisier and worse than baseline
asi.risk: This removes strict detection of extra bytes after a requested range; validate correctness assumptions before finalizing upstream
asi.next_action_hint: Rerun this exact kept change to confirm because improvement is small and workload noise is visible

description: confirmation rerun of native range-close validation change

asi.hypothesis: Repeat the previous kept native read close change to check whether the small primary improvement was stable
asi.outcome: Rerun regressed to 690.048s; previous 656.218s result was likely noise or workload variance
asi.rollback_reason: No additional code change in this iteration; do not treat the prior small improvement as confirmed
asi.next_action_hint: Consider reverting the prior commit if future runs do not show benefit; prioritize larger, safer gains

description: revert native range extra-byte validation skip

asi.hypothesis: Restoring strict native GCS range close validation may remove correctness risk and test whether the previous change was actually helping
asi.outcome: Suite was much slower at 732.229s, driven by native real_read outlier; not useful as an optimization iteration
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed significantly versus the current kept state
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the current range-close change for now as an experimental state, but revisit its correctness risk before final review

description: use 64MiB XML multipart defaults for native GCS XML writes

asi.hypothesis: Default native GCS XML multipart should use the same 64MiB single/strict part size policy that won the real-part upload benchmark, unless explicitly overridden
asi.outcome: Primary improved materially to 623.560s. Real write fell from 319.290s baseline to 230.735s, mostly because default xml real_write dropped from about 140.8s to 74.0s
asi.tradeoff: Read phases were noisy and worse in this run, but write improvement was large enough to dominate the broad suite
asi.next_action_hint: Confirm that explicit query/disk settings can still override this default; consider adding config-specific XML policy names later instead of hard-coding if needed

description: raise native GCS compose upload concurrency from 4 to 6

asi.hypothesis: A moderate native gRPC compose upload concurrency increase can reduce native real_write without the resource-pressure regression seen at 8
asi.outcome: Primary improved to 577.403s. Native real_write dropped to 71.921s, comparable to XML 64MiB writes, and aggregate native path dropped to 193.048s
asi.tradeoff: small_write regressed slightly, especially xml_64m20, likely benchmark noise or object-store contention; real_write gain dominates
asi.next_action_hint: Try native concurrency 7 or tune compose chunking only if read noise remains controlled; 8 was previously too aggressive

description: raise native GCS compose upload concurrency from 6 to 7

asi.hypothesis: Native compose upload concurrency 7 may retain write throughput while avoiding the earlier concurrency-8 resource pressure
asi.outcome: Primary improved to 566.429s, mostly from better real_read noise and small_read/native path while real_write stayed near 216s
asi.tradeoff: Native real_write was slightly slower than concurrency 6 in this run, so improvement is not purely from native upload; benchmark noise remains substantial
asi.next_action_hint: Try concurrency 8 again on top of XML default changes or focus on XML read settings; validate with repeated run before finalizing concurrency

description: raise native GCS compose upload concurrency from 7 to 8

asi.hypothesis: Concurrency 8 might improve native write further after XML default policy improvements
asi.outcome: Primary regressed from 566.429s to 573.937s. Native aggregate improved but XML real/read noise and real_write totals worsened
asi.rollback_reason: Concurrency 8 is not a broad win; previous 7 remains better for the suite
asi.next_action_hint: Keep native max_concurrent_uploads at 7 for now; avoid further simple concurrency increases

description: parallelize native GCS temporary object cleanup deletes

asi.hypothesis: Deleting native GCS compose temporary objects concurrently could reduce native write tail latency after compose
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 667.050s and real_write worsened; parallel delete did not help the broad suite
asi.rollback_reason: Likely extra thread/object-store pressure or delete phase not the bottleneck; added complexity without benefit
asi.next_action_hint: Do not parallelize cleanup this way; inspect upload/compose timing before attempting native write-tail changes

description: try 128MiB default native GCS XML multipart policy

asi.hypothesis: Larger 128MiB XML multipart chunks might further reduce part count and improve real writes compared with 64MiB defaults
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 676.787s; xml aggregate worsened sharply and real_write worsened versus 64MiB default
asi.rollback_reason: 128MiB default is too large or noisier for the broad suite; 64MiB remains the better default
asi.next_action_hint: Try 32MiB default only if exploring policy curve; otherwise keep 64MiB

description: try 32MiB default native GCS XML multipart policy

asi.hypothesis: A 32MiB XML default may trade slightly more upload parts for better read/object layout and lower memory pressure
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 633.277s; real_write worsened too much compared with 64MiB default
asi.rollback_reason: 32MiB default is not a broad win for the read/write suite
asi.next_action_hint: Keep 64MiB default; policy curve suggests 64MiB is the local optimum among 32/64/128

description: parallelize native GCS compose groups failed to compile

asi.hypothesis: Parallel first-level GCS compose operations could reduce native write tail time for large objects with many compose groups
asi.failure_mode: Build failed with -Wshadow-uncaptured-local because lambda init-captures `group` and `intermediate` shadowed local variables
asi.rollback_reason: Compile error before benchmark
asi.next_action_hint: Rename lambda captures to captured_group and captured_intermediate if retrying compose parallelism

description: parallelize native GCS intermediate compose groups

asi.hypothesis: Parallelizing independent first-level GCS compose operations could reduce native write tail latency after uploads complete
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 701.800s; real_write did not improve enough and read phases were much worse/noisy
asi.rollback_reason: Compose parallelism adds complexity and is not a broad win in the suite
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue compose parallelism without finer per-phase native write instrumentation

description: align GCS XML HTTP client connection settings with S3 disk defaults

asi.hypothesis: Setting XML multipart client max connections and keepalive parameters to S3 disk defaults could reduce XML upload overhead
asi.outcome: XML path metrics improved, but primary regressed to 630.874s due a large native real_read outlier unrelated to XML writes
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed; cannot keep on this broad suite despite promising XML secondary metrics
asi.next_action_hint: Consider retesting this change with repeated runs or a write-focused suite if XML-only optimization is desired

description: increase native GCS sequential read window multiplier from 16 to 32

asi.hypothesis: Larger native GCS range windows could reduce GET count and per-read overhead for sequential reads
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 586.100s; real_read did not improve enough and write phases were similar/noisy
asi.rollback_reason: Doubling sequential range window is not a broad win; possible extra bytes or unchanged access pattern offsets benefit
asi.next_action_hint: Do not blindly increase read windows; inspect GET count/read bytes before trying adaptive range coalescing

description: reduce native GCS sequential read window multiplier from 16 to 8

asi.hypothesis: Smaller native GCS sequential range windows may avoid over-reading and reduce latency for sparse MergeTree range reads while preserving enough streaming
asi.outcome: Primary improved slightly to 565.417s; real_read improved versus the previous kept state, but real_write was noisier/slower
asi.tradeoff: Small improvement is close to benchmark noise; confirm later before relying on it
asi.next_action_hint: Try multiplier 4 or rerun multiplier 8 for confirmation; inspect read bytes/GET counts if available

description: reduce native GCS sequential read window multiplier from 8 to 4

asi.hypothesis: Even smaller native GCS read windows might further reduce sparse-read overfetch
asi.outcome: real_read improved but real_write/native aggregate regressed heavily; primary worsened to 628.932s
asi.rollback_reason: Multiplier 4 is not a broad read/write win under the current suite
asi.next_action_hint: Keep multiplier 8; further read-window tuning should use read-focused diagnostics rather than primary suite alone

description: set native GCS sequential read window multiplier to 12

asi.hypothesis: Read window multiplier 12 might balance the overfetch reduction of 8 with fewer GETs than 8
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 580.173s versus kept multiplier 8; no clear broad benefit
asi.rollback_reason: Multiplier 12 is worse than current kept multiplier 8
asi.next_action_hint: Keep multiplier 8 as best tested among 4/8/12/16/32

description: avoid reopening native GCS streams for buffered and small forward seeks

asi.hypothesis: Mirroring S3 seek behavior in native GCS reads should reduce object stream reopen churn for MergeTree mark/range reads by seeking within buffered data or ignoring small forward gaps
asi.outcome: Primary improved materially to 540.773s. All major phase totals improved versus previous kept state, especially real_write/noise and real_read
asi.mechanism: GCSReadBuffer::seek now reuses the current buffer and reads through small forward seeks below remote_read_min_bytes_for_seek instead of always resetSequentialStream
asi.next_action_hint: Confirm with a repeat or inspect GCSReadObject counts; consider applying the same buffered-seek logic to edge cases/tests

description: confirmation rerun of native GCS buffered/small-forward seek reuse

asi.hypothesis: Repeat the kept native GCS seek reuse change to check stability
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 634.819 because xml/xml_64 real_read were outliers, but native aggregate remained good at 191.235s
asi.rollback_reason: No code change in this iteration; discard the noisy confirmation datapoint
asi.next_action_hint: The native seek change still looks plausible because native read remained strong; future benchmark should reduce XML read noise or use medians

description: retest S3-disk HTTP defaults for GCS XML client after seek optimization

asi.hypothesis: XML client S3-disk connection defaults may improve XML write paths, and previous rejection may have been native read noise
asi.outcome: Primary still regressed to 606.795. XML aggregate was decent but xml_64/native read noise and real_write did not beat current kept state
asi.rollback_reason: Not a broad win under the current benchmark
asi.next_action_hint: Do not keep HTTP default alignment unless a future write-focused benchmark justifies it separately

description: use 64MiB native GCS temporary compose objects failed to compile

asi.hypothesis: Using 64MiB native compose temporary objects could reduce native object count and compose overhead, similar to XML 64MiB policy
asi.failure_mode: Build failed because max_write_chunk_bytes became unused under -Werror after switching threshold/chunking to max_temporary_object_bytes
asi.rollback_reason: Compile error before benchmark
asi.next_action_hint: Retry by removing unused max_write_chunk_bytes or by using it in a static_assert/comment-free way if the 64MiB temp object experiment remains promising

description: 64MiB native temporary object retry missed constant declaration

asi.hypothesis: Retry 64MiB native temporary objects after removing unused max_write_chunk_bytes
asi.failure_mode: Edit did not replace the constant declaration, so max_temporary_object_bytes was undeclared while uses were changed
asi.rollback_reason: Compile error before benchmark
asi.next_action_hint: Replace the declaration line directly with max_temporary_object_bytes before rerunning

description: use 64MiB native GCS temporary compose objects

asi.hypothesis: Larger 64MiB native temporary objects should reduce compose source count and tail overhead for native large writes
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 556.284 versus current kept 540.773; native aggregate was close but real_write did not improve
asi.rollback_reason: 64MiB native temp objects are not a net win in the broad suite
asi.next_action_hint: Keep native temp objects at the Google client/service chunk size; native write appears better served by concurrency 7 and seek optimization

description: double native GCS small-forward seek threshold

asi.hypothesis: Reading through larger forward gaps could reduce native GCS stream reopen churn beyond the default remote_read_min_bytes_for_seek
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 611.018 and native aggregate worsened; more over-reading likely outweighed fewer stream resets
asi.rollback_reason: Do not multiply remote_read_min_bytes_for_seek for GCS by default
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the setting-respecting threshold; if tuning, expose a config rather than hard-code

description: halve native GCS small-forward seek threshold

asi.hypothesis: A smaller read-through threshold might avoid over-reading while still preserving buffered-seek reuse
asi.outcome: Primary regressed to 596.017; native aggregate worsened mainly from write/noise and no meaningful read win
asi.rollback_reason: Halving remote_read_min_bytes_for_seek is not a broad win
asi.next_action_hint: Keep default threshold with buffered/small-forward seek support
